requirement_text.ISS-0705: Global Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(:auto) leak in tenants_test.exs/identity_test.exs never restored to :manual, causing persistent test-DB pollution. Root cause: test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs (~line 391) and test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs (~lines 1361-1381) each flip Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) mid-test (to allow the test's own process and spawned/async work to share a connection outside the sandbox's normal per-test checkout), and never restore it to :manual afterward -- no matching on_exit callback, no restoring flip at the end of the test. Once flipped to :auto for the remainder of the test run, every subsequent test in the same mix test invocation (and, per ISS-0704's own reproduction, across separate invocations against the same persistent dev/test database) inserts real, uncontained rows instead of rows scoped to a per-test sandboxed transaction that gets rolled back. ISS-0704's diagnosis confirmed 129+ such orphaned tenant rows had accumulated in the shared test DB. Fix should either (a) wrap the :auto mode flip in each affected test with a matching on_exit callback that restores :manual, or (b) restructure the tests so they no longer need the global mode flip (e.g. using Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.allow/3 to share the sandboxed connection with a spawned process instead of disabling the sandbox outright) -- evaluate which fits each test's actual concurrency need. Operational note: the 129+ tenant rows already orphaned in the shared test DB by this leak should be identified and cleaned up as part of or alongside whatever run fixes this.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): confirmed. docs/issues/ISS-0704.yaml (status: resolved) is the matching prior entry -- it is this issue's own direct discoverer/parent: ISS-0704's resolution note explicitly names ISS-0705 as the follow-up filed for the underlying leak mechanism it deliberately left unfixed. Not a recurrence of a fix that failed to hold (ISS-0704's own fix, the pagination test's search-scoping, is unrelated code and still holds) -- this is the first attempt at the leak itself, so severity stays MAJOR as filed, not escalated.

STEP 1 (diagnose):

(a) Call-site code, quoted verbatim, with confirmation of restore behavior:

test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs:387-391 (test 'creates a tenant row, provisions a real schema, and replays real migrations'):
  # Real schema creation (CREATE SCHEMA) + migration replay needs :auto sandbox
  # mode, same as Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 -- DDL run under
  # the default per-test :manual/:shared sandbox transaction is not reliably
  # visible to Ecto.Migrator.run/4's own connection checkout.
  Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)
Read the full test body through line 432 (its on_exit at 407-418 only does DROP SCHEMA/DELETE cleanup) -- CONFIRMED: no restoring Sandbox.mode call anywhere afterward, in the test body or its on_exit. Genuinely never restored, to :manual or otherwise.

test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs:1371-1381 (describe 'REQ-076 AC6: role registry routes' setup block):
    setup do
      tenant = TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!(slug_prefix: "req076-roles")
      Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :manual)
      :ok = Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo)
      on_exit(fn -> Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) end)
      Repo.query!(~s(SET search_path TO "#{tenant.schema_name}", public))
      %{tenant: tenant}
    end
CORRECTION to the issue's own framing (Step 1's 'do not diagnose from the bug report's prose alone' -- verified by reading, not assumed): this site does NOT simply 'flip to :auto and never restore to :manual' as ISS-0705 states. It flips to :manual (line 1374) + a fresh checkout (1375) -- the ordinary safe pattern -- runs the whole test body under a real per-test sandboxed transaction, and its on_exit (1381) then flips back to :auto, not :manual. This is not accidental: it is a verbatim mirror of test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs's own established, already-in-the-tree pattern (that file's setup at lines 101-119 does the exact same 'provisioned_tenant! (which itself leaves mode at :auto per its own moduledoc, ISS-0113/INV-F-6) -> flip to :manual+checkout -> run test -> on_exit forces :auto back on' shape, with role_registry_test.exs's own on_exit comment stating it 'mirrors identity_test.exs's own on_exit/1 handling of this exact hazard, confirmed empirically there'). The reason both force :auto in on_exit rather than leaving :manual: on_exit runs in ExUnit's separate OnExitHandler process (not the original test process), so a lingering :manual-mode checkout tied to the now-dead test process cannot serve the DROP SCHEMA/DELETE cleanup that TenantFixture's own on_exit (registered earlier, so it runs AFTER this one, LIFO) needs -- forcing :auto first guarantees that cleanup gets a real, checked-in connection. So: CONFIRMED it never restores to :manual, but that is not itself the defect at this call site -- ending at :auto matches the ambient convention TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 itself establishes and role_registry_test.exs already uses identically. The actual hazard here is the same one ISS-0580 already named and fixed for six OTHER call sites (lib/letflow/design/iss0580-sandbox-auto-mode-restore-leak.md): while ANY of these on_exit callbacks holds the pool at :auto (even briefly, for the DROP SCHEMA/DELETE window), concurrently-running async:true tests' ordinary Repo writes commit for real instead of rolling back. identity_test.exs's block (and role_registry_test.exs's identical one) were not among ISS-0580's six fixed files, and don't use its new test/support/sandbox_auto_mode.ex helper -- so this is an existing gap in that same closed issue's coverage, not a distinct new bug shape.

(b) Other call sites (repo-wide grep for `Sandbox.mode(...:auto)`, run and reviewed in full): far more than the two named in this issue. Confirmed additional non-restoring or self-restoring sites in: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:228 (TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 itself -- deliberately unrestored per its own moduledoc, 'ISS-0113, out of scope; INV-F-6'), test/support/sandbox_auto_mode.ex (the ISS-0580 helper module itself: provision!/2 self-restores via try/after; enter_auto_mode!/1 + exit_auto_mode!/1 are the deferred-restore pair used by test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs), test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs:102 + :157 + :119 (the exact mirror analyzed above), test/support/exam_fixtures.ex:68, test/support/tenant_template.ex:105, test/support/tenant_slug.ex (documented, not a live call), test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:150/225 (paired with :manual restores at :202/:273 inside after-blocks -- self-restoring, ISS-0580-style), test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs and test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs (multiple sites, several with adjacent :manual restores, some without -- not fully audited line-by-line since out of this issue's owned_modules, but flagged for CODE-DESIGNER as evidence the restore/non-restore pattern is inconsistent project-wide, not confined to the two named files), test/support/tenant_template_test.exs:59, test/support/tenant_template_retry_test.exs:61, test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs:60. None of these extra sites are in this issue's affected_files/owned_modules, so no fix is proposed for them here -- listed only because the issue's own acceptance criteria required the full-repo grep, and because CODE-DESIGNER should know the two named files are not the only instances of this shape before designing a fix pattern that might generalize.

(c) Real orphaned-tenant-row count, queried directly against the live test DB (docker container letflow-postgres-1, port 5462 per config/db_port.exs/.env, via `MIX_ENV=test mix run -e` against Letflow.Repo -- no MIX_TEST_PARTITION override needed, default `letflow_test` database): SELECT count(*) FROM tenants -> 129 (exact, not '129+'; matches ISS-0704's estimate almost exactly, meaning the count has been essentially static since ISS-0704's own run, not still climbing every mix test invocation since -- consistent with async:false module scheduling limiting the collision window in practice, discussed below). Grouped by slug prefix (stripped of trailing UUID/unique-integer suffixes) to identify origin: ZERO rows have the 'req075' (tenants_test.exs) or 'req076' (identity_test.exs) prefixes used by those two files' own fixtures -- their own on_exit cleanup is confirmed working. The 129 rows are ALL attributable to unrelated test files: the large majority (>60 rows) are 'req332-*'/'req333-*' prefixes from test/letflow/exam/anti_cheat_test.exs (also async:false, uses TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1, itself never calls Sandbox.mode directly), plus smaller counts under 'iss0631-*', 'iss0648-ac12-*', 'req053', 'req331-inv1', 'iss0414-tenant', and one 'verify-dup-tag'. IMPORTANT correction to the issue's premise: fixing the two named call sites' own restore behavior will NOT retroactively explain or prevent this specific 129-row backlog, because none of those 129 rows were left by tenants_test.exs or identity_test.exs's own fixtures -- they are collateral from OTHER tests' ordinary provisioned_tenant!/1 usage running under the ambient :auto state that TenantFixture itself establishes and (per ISS-0113/INV-F-6) is not supposed to restore. The operational cleanup ISS-0705 asks for (deleting the 129 rows) is real and still needed, but is logically independent of whichever of the two named call sites gets fixed.

Per-file fix recommendation:

- test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs:391 -- RECOMMEND (a)-shaped fix using the EXISTING ISS-0580 helper rather than a hand-rolled on_exit: wrap the real-provisioning segment (the dispatch() call through the information_schema check, lines ~391-431) with `Letflow.Test.SandboxAutoMode.provision!/2` (test/support/sandbox_auto_mode.ex:62-72), which already does exactly 'enter :auto, run fun, restore :manual + fresh checkout in an after-block' in the SAME process. This fits because the whole test runs in one process (dispatch is direct `Letflow.Routers.Tenants.call/2`, not a spawned Task -- confirmed by the file's own moduledoc, line 13) with no cross-process connection-sharing need, so allow/3 (which exists to let a SEPARATE process use the calling process's checked-out connection) does not apply here -- there is no separate process to allow. provision!/2's self-restoring, try/after shape is the designed-for fit, and reusing it (rather than inventing a new bespoke on_exit) matches the helper module's own moduledoc instruction to 'build from it, don't invent a different shape.'

- test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs:1371-1381 -- RECOMMEND (b), but not allow/3 either (same reasoning: no spawned process in this describe block) -- restructure using the OTHER half of the same ISS-0580 helper, `exit_auto_mode!/1` (test/support/sandbox_auto_mode.ex:107-110), in place of the inline `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` at line 1381, registered as the FIRST on_exit per that function's own doc ('Register this as the first-registered on_exit/1 callback... before any existing cleanup on_exit that still needs :auto mode active'). This does not change the end-state (still :auto, matching TenantFixture's own ambient convention -- restoring to :manual instead would be WRONG per ISS-0113/INV-F-6, contradicting the issue's own literal 'restore to :manual' framing) but closes the actual gap: this call site, and role_registry_test.exs's byte-for-byte identical one, were not included in ISS-0580's six-file fix and don't use its shared helper. CODE-DESIGNER should treat role_registry_test.exs's matching setup block (lines 101-163) as an in-scope companion fix even though it's outside this issue's own affected_files/owned_modules -- flagging this explicitly rather than silently expanding scope myself.

Summary for CODE-DESIGNER: this is two related but distinct problems, not one. (1) tenants_test.exs:391 has a genuine, simple never-restored leak -- fix with SandboxAutoMode.provision!/2. (2) identity_test.exs:1371-1381 already restores to the same INTENTIONAL ambient state (:auto) the rest of the suite relies on, mirroring an existing, already-reviewed pattern (role_registry_test.exs) -- the real gap is that this shape isn't yet using the ISS-0580 helper that exists for exactly this case; fix by swapping in exit_auto_mode!/1, and treat role_registry_test.exs as a paired fix. (3) The 129 already-orphaned rows are NOT from either named file and must be identified/deleted as a separate operational step (a one-off DELETE keyed on the confirmed non-req075/req076 prefixes above, or more simply: any tenant row whose slug does not match a currently-running test's own fixture naming, since a clean test DB should hold zero tenant rows between mix test invocations) -- doing so does not depend on, and is not accomplished by, either code fix above.
issues: Call-site count and shape: tenants_test.exs:391 is a plain unrestored leak; identity_test.exs:1371-1381 restores to :auto (matching an existing project-wide convention) rather than never restoring at all, so ISS-0705's 'never restore to :manual' framing does not literally apply to that site the way it does to tenants_test.exs -- see full reasoning in summary.

role_registry_test.exs (test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs:101-163) has a byte-for-byte identical pattern to identity_test.exs's call site and is not in this issue's affected_files -- recommend CODE-DESIGNER treat it as a paired fix rather than leaving it inconsistent with identity_test.exs post-fix.

The 129 orphaned tenant rows counted are NOT attributable to either of this issue's two named files (0 rows with req075/req076 prefixes) -- they come from unrelated test files (anti_cheat_test.exs and others).
